The grade on each product page is the grade in the certificate, stated per SKU and never inferred. Concentration and grade are separate choices — most strengths from 5% to 85% are stocked in more than one grade, so pick the grade your specification requires first, then the strength your process wants.

### Why 75% exists — and when to buy it over 85%

85% phosphoric acid is the standard commercial concentrate, but it begins to crystallize around 70 °F — a drum stored in an unheated warehouse or shipped in winter can arrive partly solid. 75% stays liquid far below freezing, which is why cold-climate plants and winter buyers specify it — and it is cheaper per drum. If your process is water-sensitive and needs maximum P₂O₅ per gallon, take 85% and store it warm; if handling temperature is outside your control, 75% is the practical choice.

## Frequently Asked Questions

What is phosphoric acid used for?  

Phosphoric acid is used for rust conversion, metal treatment, food and beverage acidulation, pH adjustment, cleaning, descaling, and industrial process chemistry.

  What is the difference between food grade and technical grade phosphoric acid?  

Food or USP grades are selected when a regulated food, beverage, or formulation process requires that specification. Technical grade is used for industrial cleaning, pH control, and metal treatment where food-grade documentation is not required.

  Can phosphoric acid remove rust?  

Yes. Phosphoric acid can convert iron oxide and support rust-removal workflows on compatible metal surfaces when concentration, contact time, and rinsing are controlled.

  Is phosphoric acid an oxidizing acid?  

Phosphoric acid is generally considered a non-oxidizing mineral acid, unlike nitric acid. It is still corrosive and requires acid-rated handling controls.

  Does phosphoric acid require hazmat shipping?  

Shipping requirements depend on concentration, package size, destination, and transport mode. Review the product SDS and order details for the applicable classification.

## What Is Phosphoric Acid?

Phosphoric acid, alongside nitrogen and [potassium](https://us.metoree.com/categories/6882), is one of the three primary elements of fertilizer and an oxoacid of phosphorus.

Also known as orthophosphoric acid, it promotes flowering and fruiting in plants and is a crucial component of DNA and RNA, the genetic material, and cell membranes in living organisms. Phosphoric acid is essential for life.

As a natural resource, phosphorus is found as phosphate ore, and its depletion is concerning. Phosphoric acid is industrially produced through two methods: dry and wet.

### Uses of Phosphoric Acid

Phosphoric acid is widely used in industry as a raw material for various phosphates, chemical polishing agents for aluminum, rust inhibitors for metals, metal cleaning agents, can cleaners, refractory auxiliaries, paint preparation agents, activated sludge processes, [phosphate fertilizers](https://us.metoree.com/categories/7683), and reagents.

In food applications, it serves as an acidifier for beverages, a pH adjuster in brewing, and a raw material for phosphoric acid additives in juices, colas, and other food products.

It is also utilized as a raw material for dyeing auxiliaries, petrochemical catalysts, and pharmaceutical additives.

### Properties of Phosphoric Acid

Phosphoric acid has a melting point of 42.35°C and a boiling point of 407°C. When melted, it appears as a clear, colorless liquid.

It is soluble in water, alcohol, and ether. Liquid anhydrous phosphoric acid is a strong acid and a high conductor of electricity.

### Structure of Phosphoric Acid

The chemical formula of phosphoric acid is H3PO4. Its molar mass is 98.00 g/mol, and its density at 25°C is 1.892. Pure phosphoric acid forms unstable crystals of the orthorhombic system.

Phosphoric acid ions adopt a tetrahedral structure. The bond distance between phosphorus and oxygen (P-O) in aluminum phosphoric acid crystals is 152 pm.

### Other Information on Phosphoric Acid

#### 1. Synthesis of Phosphoric Acid

Burning phosphorus produces diphosphorus pentoxide, which, when dissolved in a dilute aqueous solution of phosphoric acid, yields pure phosphoric acid. This thermal synthesis method is environmentally friendly, although impurities in the mined phosphorus must be removed.

Phosphoric acid can also be obtained by reacting approximately 35% [sulfuric acid](https://us.metoree.com/categories/6704) with phosphate ore. This wet synthesis method can be purified through filtration, but may contain impurities such as hydrofluoric acid, resulting in lower purity than the thermal synthesis method.

#### 2. Structure of Phosphoric Acid Ion

![Figure 2. Structure of phosphate ion](https://metoree.com/wpdrs/wp-content/uploads/2023/01/6558_Phosphoric-Acid_リン酸-2.png)

![Figure 2. Structure of phosphate ion](https://metoree.com/wpdrs/wp-content/uploads/2023/01/6558_Phosphoric-Acid_リン酸-2.png)

**Figure 2. Structure of Phosphoric Acid Ion**

Phosphoric acid, a trivalent acid, ionizes in aqueous solution, releasing three hydrogen ions. The ionization stages produce dihydrogen phosphate (H2PO4-), hydrogen phosphate (HPO42-), and phosphate (PO43-) ions.

The pKa values at 25°C are pKa1 = 2.12, pKa2 = 7.21, and pKa3 = 12.67, respectively.

#### 3. Dehydration Reaction of Phosphoric Acid

![Figure 3. Structure of condensed phosphoric acid](https://metoree.com/wpdrs/wp-content/uploads/2023/01/6558_Phosphoric-Acid_リン酸-3.png)

![Figure 3. Structure of condensed phosphoric acid](https://metoree.com/wpdrs/wp-content/uploads/2023/01/6558_Phosphoric-Acid_リン酸-3.png)

**Figure 3. Structure of Condensed Phosphoric Acid**

Upon heating, phosphoric acid undergoes a dehydration reaction. At 150°C, it becomes anhydrous, and at 200°C, two molecules react to form pyrophosphoric acid. Higher temperatures lead to the formation of meta-phosphoric acid, a condensed compound, when one water molecule per phosphoric acid unit is desorbed. Diphosphorus pentoxide, produced by further dehydration, reacts violently with water and is used as a drying agent.

#### 4. Phosphoric Acid and Health

Phosphorus, found in foods of biological origin such as vegetables and meat, is used as an acidity additive in foods and beverages. It is a necessary mineral for the human body, with recommended daily amounts set by health authorities.

## Phosphoric acid

ICL is a leading producer of phosphoric acid for chemical manufacturing. ICL’s Polyphosphoric Acid (PPA) is supplied as raw material and recommended for use or evaluation in the following manufacturing processes: production of flame retardants phosphate esters, phosphorylation of polyols, production of phosphate ester surfactants, as a catalyst in organic reactions, and improving thermo-mechanical properties of asphalt cements.

## Product Overview

Phosphoric Acid 75% USP Food Grade is a clear, colorless, odorless viscous liquid — orthophosphoric acid (H₃PO₄, CAS 7664-38-2) at 75% concentration in a food-grade specification. It is the workhorse acid for buyers who need acidity control in food and beverage processing, phosphorus chemistry in fertilizer blending, or rust and scale removal in maintenance cleaning, and who need food-grade documentation behind it. we distribute it in our Taylor, TX warehouse and ship it daily, from single quarts for bench work up to 330-gallon totes for production lines.

## Why This Concentration

At 75%, this product carries serious acid strength while pouring and metering more easily than the most concentrated grades. Phosphoric acid gets noticeably more viscous as concentration climbs; 75% stays fluid enough to pump and dose accurately at room temperature, which matters when you are feeding a pH-control loop or blending it into a formulation. It is still a corrosive liquid with the signal word Danger — it causes severe skin burns and eye damage and may be corrosive to metals (per the product's GHS classification) — so treat it with the same respect you would give any strong acid.

Pick this concentration when you want fewer dilution steps than a weaker solution requires, but easier handling than a more concentrated acid demands. The Food Grade designation matters when your process touches food, beverage, or similar regulated formulations; if your application is strictly industrial — say, rust removal on shop equipment — a technical grade may serve at lower cost, and this page's grade is the right call only when food-grade quality is a requirement, not a preference.

## Chemical Profile

This is a clear, colorless viscous liquid with no odor. The formula is H₃PO₄ with a molecular weight of 97.995, registered under CAS 7664-38-2. Density of the 75% solution runs approximately 1.575 at 25 °C — noticeably heavier than water, which you feel the moment you lift a full gallon jug. It is miscible with water, so dilution to working strength is straightforward: it blends completely without layering or settling. Vapor pressure is low, meaning it does not fume aggressively at ambient temperature the way volatile mineral acids do, though ventilation in storage and handling areas is still standard practice.

## Industrial Applications

Phosphoric acid at this strength and grade shows up across several industries:

* **pH adjustment in food processing** — dosed to bring product and process water acidity to target, supporting flavor development and preservation chemistry in formulations.
* **Beverage acidulation** — the classic acidulant behind the tart bite in soft drinks and other beverages, metered into syrup and blending operations.
* **Fertilizer and agriculture** — a phosphorus source for liquid fertilizer blending, supplying one of the three primary plant nutrients.
* **Rust and scale removal** — converts iron oxide and dissolves mineral deposits in industrial cleaning formulations, which is why it anchors many metal-prep and descaling products.
* **Pharmaceutical buffering** — used in formulation work to hold pH stable in buffered systems.

In every one of these, the acid is doing process chemistry — donating protons, supplying phosphate, converting oxides. Your own process qualification determines fit; the technical data sheet and lot documentation give you the specification data to run that qualification.

## Handling & Storage

The signal word is Danger. This product causes severe skin burns and eye damage (H314) and may be corrosive to metals (H290) (per the product's GHS classification). Handle it accordingly: chemical-resistant gloves, splash goggles or a face shield, and clothing that covers exposed skin. Keep an eyewash accessible wherever it is dispensed.

Store it in HDPE or glass — the same materials we pack it in — away from incompatible materials, heat, and direct light. Because it can attack metals, do not transfer it into unlined steel containers or leave it in contact with metal fittings. It is stable in storage under those conditions; low vapor pressure means it is not pushing fumes into your storage area, but keep the space ventilated as a matter of course. Ground-level storage for larger containers saves your team from lifting a dense liquid overhead: a gallon of this product weighs roughly half again what a gallon of water does.

## How Innophos Processes Purified Phosphoric Acid

Innophos processes phosphoric acid through a series of advanced chemical engineering steps, ensuring high purity and consistency for its various applications. The typical process includes the following steps:  
   
 **1. Raw Material Selection:** Innophos sources phosphate rock, a natural mineral, as the primary raw material.  
   
 **2. Acidulation:**After being shipped to a manufacturing facility, the phosphate rock undergoes processing with sulfuric acid in large reactors, producing phosphoric acid. This process is known as the wet-process method. The wet process is favored due to its lower energy consumption and cost-effectiveness.  
   
 **3. Purification:** After the initial phosphoric acid is created, it then goes through a process to remove impurities. This process involves filtration and chemical treatments to ensure the final product meets specific purity standards required for different applications, such as food, technical, or industrial grades.  
   
 **4. Concentration:** The purified phosphoric acid is concentrated through evaporation. This step increases the acid's concentration to desired levels, usually around 75% to 85% H3PO4 for various industrial and food-grade uses.  
   
 **5. Quality:**Throughout the process, Innophos employs stringent quality and food safety control measures, including regular testing and analysis, to ensure the product meets the necessary specifications and regulatory requirements. For food grade products, [our manufacturing operations](/who-we-are/about-us/manufacturing-capabilities) meet Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP), and [all manufacturing sites](/who-we-are/about-us/our-locations) have Global Food Safety Initiative (GFSI) certification. Additionally, Innophos has robust preventive controls in place to meet the requirements of the Food Safety Modernization Act (FSMA).  
   
 **6. Packaging and Distribution:**The final phosphoric acid product is then packaged in appropriate containers, ranging from bulk tanks for industrial use to smaller containers for food-grade applications, and distributed to customers.  
   
 These steps ensure that Innophos provides high-quality phosphoric acid suitable for a range of uses, from food & beverage or other industrial applications.
